data.title: A place to slow down.
data.intro: sādhana is a small, independent yoga studio. We teach thoughtful classes in a bright, welcoming space, for every body.

children.text: sādhana is a Sanskrit word for a daily practice. We chose it because the idea is simple: a little time, most days, spent on something that makes you feel more at home in yourself.

We opened with two rooms, a handful of teachers and a belief that a studio should feel like a living room more than a gym. Mats are always available, nobody is expected to know the poses and everyone is welcome to rest.
How we teach
Plain language, clear options and no pressure
Classes for beginners through to experienced students
Small groups so teachers can see everyone
What we do not do

We do not promise cures or results, and we do not ask you to push through discomfort. Yoga here is about attention, breath and movement. If you have a medical condition or an injury, please talk to your doctor and let your teacher know before class.
Our space
Two rooms, both with wooden floors and plenty of daylight: the Sun room and the Garden room. We keep a stack of blankets, bolsters and blocks in each.

data.title: Studio guide
data.intro: A few small things that make class easier for everyone.

children.text: Arriving
Please arrive five to ten minutes early for your first class so we can show you around. Late arrivals may be asked to join the next class.
Cancelling
Let us know at least four hours before class if you cannot make it, so we can offer the place to someone else.
Phones and quiet
Please silence phones before you enter the room. Our rooms are shared quiet spaces.
Injuries and conditions
Tell your teacher about any injury or condition before class. We cannot give medical advice and encourage you to consult a doctor if you are unsure.

data.title: Sunset Unwind
data.summary: Why every class at sādhana begins slowly, and what a few quiet minutes can do for the rest of the hour.

children.text: Walk into most studios and you will find the first few minutes are the busiest: mats unrolling, shoes coming off, a handful of people still arriving. We like to treat that stretch as part of class.
A soft landing
Each class starts with a short, seated pause. We ask nothing of you except to arrive. Some people close their eyes; others look out of the window. Both are fine.
Starting slowly also means the warm-up does real work. Moving gently at first lets you notice where you feel tight, where you feel strong and what you might want to change today.

data.title: Sunset Unwind
data.summary: A friendly guide to picking a first class, what to wear and how to get the most out of it.

children.text: If this is your first time in a yoga studio, welcome. A few small decisions can make your first visit easier.
Start with a beginner class
Slow Flow for Beginners and Gentle Hatha are good places to begin. The pace is easy to follow and every pose comes with options.
What to bring
A water bottle
Clothes you can move in
An open mind. That is it.
We have mats, blocks, straps and blankets, so there is nothing to buy first.

data.title: Sunset Unwind
data.summary: Blocks, bolsters and blankets are not a sign of anything except that you want to be comfortable.

children.text: In our studio, props are for everyone. A cork block can bring the floor closer to your hands. A bolster can make a long rest feel generous.
A few of our favourites
Blocks under the hands in standing poses
A folded blanket beneath the hips when sitting
A bolster under the knees when lying down
Ask any teacher and they will happily show you a new way to use them.

data.title: Sunset Unwind
data.summary: Three simple ways to pause and breathe during an ordinary day, no mat required.

children.text: You do not need a studio to take a breath. These are three small habits we share with new students.
Three small pauses
Before you open your laptop, take three slow breaths
Between meetings, let your shoulders drop
Before bed, breathe out a little longer than you breathe in
None of this replaces anything. It is simply a quiet moment you can come back to.

data.title: Sunset Unwind
data.summary: A short tour of the two rooms we teach in, and how we decide which class goes where.

children.text: We have two rooms. The Sun room is larger and faces the street, with tall windows and warm wooden floors. The Garden room is smaller, quieter and lit with lamps in the evening.
Which class where
Flowing classes tend to live in the Sun room; restorative and breath classes in the Garden room. If you would like a particular room, just ask.
